key_insight: The Asta Interaction Dataset provides the first large-scale, real-world view of how researchers use LLM-powered, retrieval-augmented scientific tools — revealing common behaviors like iterative querying, distinct use patterns across literature discovery vs. question answering, and opportunities to improve retrieval and UI design.
problem_solved: Lack of empirical, large-scale evidence about real researcher interactions with AI-powered scientific tools that hinders informed design, evaluation, and benchmarking of retrieval-augmented LLM systems for research workflows.
method: Collect and aggregate over 200,000 anonymized user queries and interaction logs from two deployed tools (literature discovery and scientific QA) within a retrieval-augmented generation platform.
Annotate and analyze usage patterns, session dynamics, query reformulations, and differences between the two tool types to derive a taxonomy of researcher behaviors.
Release the dataset (with privacy safeguards) to enable reproducible studies, UX research, and improved evaluation of RAG/LLM research tooling.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners, HCI researchers, and tool designers with empirical evidence to prioritize improvements in retrieval, response grounding, and interface workflows; enables development and benchmarking of models and UIs tuned to real scientific search and QA behaviors.
visual_elements: Overview schematic of the RAG platform showing literature discovery and QA interfaces feeding into a shared retrieval + LLM backend (architecture diagram).
Session timeline heatmap illustrating typical interaction cadence, query reformulation rates, and duration distributions (timeline/heatmap).
Stacked bar chart comparing query intents and outcomes across the two tool types (explore vs. answer), including proportions of iterative vs. one-shot queries.
Flow diagram / taxonomy of common user behaviors (search → refine → synthesize → cite) with icons for actions and recommended design interventions.
paper_title: Understanding Usage and Engagement in AI-Powered Scientific Research Tools: The Asta Interaction Dataset
paper_authors: Dany Haddad, Dan Bareket, Joseph Chee Chang, Jay DeYoung, Jena D. Hwang
